bw-surface.$description:
The line goes, and unlike the figure/ground voice nothing arrives to replace it.
That is the whole claim: what belongs together is near, what does not is far, and the reader is
trusted to see distance without being shown an edge.

This alone is not proximity, which is why the gate asks for the other two as well. A voice that
removed the line and kept a fill, or kept a depth, would be grouping by region or by figure and
ground with the hairline turned off.

fill-surface.$description:
The card takes the page's own fill, so it stops being a card. A fill is a region
drawn however faint it is: base-200 against base-100 measures 1.07:1 in dark and 1.10:1 in light,
which is nearly invisible and still reads as a container once it has a corner and padding around
it. Nearly invisible is the wrong target here. The target is absent.

fill-surface-floating is deliberately untouched. A menu, a dialog and a toast are separated from
what they cover rather than grouped against it, so they keep a fill of their own; a voice that
flattened them too would have made every overlay unreadable to win an argument about cards. That
split is the reason the two fill roles exist.

pad-surface.$description:
A surface with no line, no depth and no fill has no inside, so it has no room to
give: its content sits on the page directly and lines up with everything else that does. Padding
here would be an indent nobody asked for, and an indent is a weak enclosure, which is the thing
this voice spent its other three decisions removing.

The floating tier has no padding role at all, which is what keeps a dialog from collapsing onto
its own edges when this value goes to zero.

rhythm-group.$description:
Tighter than the default, and that is half of the mechanism. Proximity says two
things are one by putting them near each other, so near has to be nearer than it needs to be when
a box is doing the work as well.

rhythm-component.$description:
Two peer components separated by twice the air inside one of them is not a step a
reader sees, and this voice has no line to fall back on when the distance fails. Widened until
the ladder reads: 8px inside a group, 24px between peers, 64px between sections, which is 1 to 3
to 8. The default ladder can afford to be gentler because a hairline is carrying the grouping
beside it.

rhythm-section.$description:
The far end of the ladder. 8px inside a group against 64px between sections is a ratio of
eight, where the default is two and the figure/ground voice is a little over three. Distance is
the ONLY signal this voice has left, so it has to carry a hierarchy that the other two spend
lines, fills and shadows on, and a ratio that reads as a hierarchy is what pays for the edge that
is no longer drawn. check:extensions holds it above four for exactly that reason.
